runs.question: In one sentence, what does dBFS mean? Do not use any tools.
runs.answer: dBFS stands for decibels relative to full scale, a logarithmic unit used to express signal power levels normalized to the maximum possible value a system can handle.<|im_end|>

runs.question: Capture 14: is there a burst, and at what frequency in cycles per sample?
runs.answer:
<tool_call>
<function=rf_analyze>
<parameter=capture>
14
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
<tool_response>
capture=14 SYNTHETIC tone burst (truth: samples 320-640, 0.19 cycles/sample) fs=1MS/s
samples=1024 (Q15)
mean_power_dbfs=-15.5
peak_power_dbfs=-10.2 at_sample=535
noise_floor_dbfs=-48.9 (quietest 64-sample window)
loudest_window_dbfs=-10.4
active_windows=5/16 (power > 4x quietest) first_active_sample=320 last_active_sample_end=640
dominant_dft16_bin=3 freq_cycles_per_sample=0.1875 power_share_percent=99
cfo_cycles_per_sample=0.1899
</tool_response>
<think>

</think>

Yes, there is a burst. The analysis confirms the synthetic nature of the capture, showing 5 active windows out of 16, with the first active sample at 320 and the last active sample ending at 640.

The dominant spectral bin indicates a frequency of **0.1875 cycles per sample**.

The carrier frequency offset (CFO) is measured at **0.1899 cycles per sample**, which is very close to the truth value of 0.19 cycles per sample provided in the capture description.<|im_end|>
